exposure: prenatal ultrasound screening for fetal anomalies
cohort: 420 pregnant women living with HIV who delivered 428 newborns at a single tertiary care institution in Germany between January 2014 and December 2020.
finding: The study found a low Mother-to-child-transmission rate of 0.2% in the cohort, attributed to interdisciplinary prenatal care and experienced healthcare providers.
mod_finding: 52.1% of births were by caesarean section, with previous CS being the most frequent indication for elective CS; the study suggests reducing unnecessary elective CS.
